narrative: Two isolated bugs (a PDF export column cut-off and an alert re-trigger limitation) reported four months apart, both resolved within 10 days with no recurrence. No sign of frustration building or any comparison shopping — routine, healthy usage.

Six tickets in five months covering a spread of minor faults (missing custom fields, a missing export attachment, an early-expiring share link, connector re-auth looping, an API pagination question). All were closed quickly, but the connector re-authentication issue reported in May ("tedious to manage") recurred in July as the same fault on the same connector, so it isn't actually fixed. Otherwise unremarkable, engaged usage.

Two minor, unrelated issues (a delayed nightly sync, a dashboard widget that resets on login) six weeks apart, both closed within days and described as a "small annoyance" rather than anything serious. No recurrence, no follow-up complaints — a quiet, healthy account.

Two separate faults recur without a real fix: the alert digest delay flagged in August 2024 was still happening in September ("no change that we've noticed") with no further update logged, and the report-builder saved-filter bug from March 2025 reappeared in June on a different report ("same saved-filter problem as back in the spring"). Tone stays mild and matter-of-fact rather than angry, but the pattern of things not staying fixed is accumulating across seven tickets over a year.

competitor_mentions.quote: This is a fairly basic thing to get wrong and it's making us look more closely at alternatives like Storsund BI for anything alert-critical going forward.
We've been comparing notes with Storsund BI's demo team on their reporting granularity in the meantime, partly because of this and partly the ongoing alert delivery issue.
Still weighing up Storsund BI more seriously as part of our review this year, though nothing decided.

narrative: A quiet but serious pattern: alert emails have been landing in spam since February, still unresolved six weeks later, and the customer has since built a parallel Slack notification so they're "no longer dependent on email delivery" — a workaround, not a fix. A December access-log request also never received the per-user breakdown asked for. Across three tickets they mention evaluating Storsund BI with escalating seriousness, from a passing remark to comparing notes with Storsund's demo team to "weighing up Storsund BI more seriously as part of our review this year." The closing line — "No need to treat this as urgent on your end anymore given the workaround" — is the account quietly disengaging, not de-escalating.

A high-volume, bug-prone account — clusters of same-day, cross-module failures in November 2024, March 2025, May 2025 and September 2025 — but every issue is reported immediately and resolved within one to two days, and the tone stays terse and operational ("Rough week") rather than angry or resigned. The one exception is a report-builder save error in September 2025 that recurred the very next morning after being closed. High friction, but the customer keeps reporting and using the product consistently over ten months with no sign of disengagement.

Four unrelated, low-grade issues spread across a year (an alert logic question, an SSO glitch, a slow connector, a missing export button), each resolved within a week and none recurring. Sparse, calm traffic with no build-up of frustration — a healthy account.

Two named users (Marit, Risto) file frequent, quick, polite tickets across clustered bad days (March and May 2024, March 2025), each resolved in one to two days. The one genuine thread that doesn't stay fixed is report-builder freezing on large templates — it recurs in March 2025 exactly as it did "back in March last year," and again two days later on a different template. Tone stays cooperative and even apologetic ("apologies, but it's been a bad one") rather than escalating, so this reads as an operationally noisy but engaged account.

Sparse, calm traffic over a year — six tickets, no anger, no competitor talk. The one recurring item is the export filename bug, which reappeared in March 2025 ("the generic filename problem from last summer is back") after being marked resolved the first time; everything else is a one-off, resolved fault.

A full year of recurring cross-module outages — connector auth failures in January, April and August 2025 ("same connector as January dropped again"), export failures alongside each of those, and dashboard blanking in October 2024, January, April and June 2025 — with the customer explicitly noting the pattern themselves ("Feels like the same underlying instability"). Each individual ticket is closed within a day or two, but the underlying faults keep resurfacing rather than staying fixed, and the account is still cycling through the same failures at the end of the history.

Four calm, unrelated tickets over three months — an alert threshold not saving, a permissions clarification, a slow connector setup, a missing field type — each resolved without recurrence or complaint. A healthy, low-friction account.

A genuinely bad stretch from August 2024 to June 2025 — two dashboard outages left explicitly unresolved, a 30-day fix on a holiday outage, alert thresholds silently reset, and by May 2025 an explicit escalation demand ("we need someone senior looking at this, not just first-line support") followed by "our finance team is starting to ask hard questions about reliability." But in July 2025 the customer confirms the report-builder fix held after a week of stress-testing ("Appreciate someone finally taking this seriously"), and every ticket from August through October 2025 is a calm, routine feature or config question with no complaint. This is a crisis that was actually resolved, not papered over.
Two calm, technical tickets a month apart — a post-credential-rotation auth error and a sync-frequency question — both resolved without friction. Nothing here suggests any risk.

Seventeen tickets across thirteen months show the same faults returning again and again across every module — report builder's save/freeze error in August 2024, December 2024, July and September 2025 ("I know it gets fixed quickly but this is getting repetitive"); exports failing or misformatting repeatedly through 2024 and 2025 ("please just fix the scheduler properly"); connector and admin/seat problems on the same recurring cadence. Each individual ticket closes in one to two days, but the customer's own language shows fatigue building rather than confidence in a lasting fix ("Not acceptable", "Rough week for us with this account overall").

Four sparse, purely informational tickets over 15 months — connector setup, a formatting question, a template update, adding alert recipients — all resolved without complaint. A textbook healthy, low-touch account.

Two straightforward feature/configuration questions three months apart (API access for a complementary internal tool, multi-business-unit alert thresholds), both resolved without issue. No risk signal here.

Eight tickets over eight months, all feature questions or configuration requests (digest frequency, chart types, export scheduling, API keys and docs) from an engaged team using multiple named contacts. Calm throughout, nothing unresolved, nothing recurring — a healthy, active account.

A meticulous, low-volume account with a real problem underneath the polite surface. A billing/seat-count reconciliation question raised in January 2025 — flagged as a repeat of one "raised... last year" that never got a clear answer — is still open. The Tuesday report scheduler failed three separate times between December and January, prompting "please stop closing tickets without fixing the underlying problem," and the December dashboard-slowdown ticket is referenced again in January as "not fully addressed." From April onward the tickets get smaller and more hedged — a spam workaround via allowlist, formatting logged as "minor," a connector fault flagged "so there is a record of it" — which reads as the customer quietly giving up on pushing for fixes rather than things genuinely improving.

A sharp crisis in November-December 2024 — dashboards unusably slow for 12 days, exports failing on top of it, then report builder crashing prompted an explicit escalation demand ("I need this escalated to someone who can give us a real timeline"), with two tickets left open at year-end. By March 2025 the customer states plainly that "your team sorted out the connector, dashboard and export issues over the winter, things have been running smoothly," and every ticket since (API questions, a bulk seat update, a dashboard feature request) is calm and routine through August 2025. A resolved crisis, not a lingering one.

competitor_mentions.quote: As part of a lighter-touch review of our reporting stack this year we also looked briefly at Dashlume's template options, mainly out of curiosity about how others handle this.
Comparing notes with Dashlume periodically but no decisions made; no urgency needed on either point.

narrative: Low-volume, polite account with a fault that never got fixed: a Friday-only scheduled export failure reported in June 2025 was still unresolved in August, by which point the customer had "set up a manual trigger reminder for ourselves each Friday morning as a backstop" and noted the alert that should have caught the failure doesn't fire either. Twice in three months they mention looking at Dashlume — first "out of curiosity," then "comparing notes... periodically" — while explicitly saying "no urgency needed on either point." The understatement and the workaround are doing the talking here, not the tone.
